key_insight: MemPilot lets an LLM agent decide at runtime when to reuse stored memory versus curate raw multimodal history, balancing quality, cost, and latency on demand.
engineering_relevance: This framework is relevant for building deployable multimodal agents because it converts memory handling into a controllable runtime policy rather than a fixed preprocessing pipeline.
method: RL-trained multi-step policy selects between retrieval and query-specific curation.
Policy controls evidence amount, curation instructions, model choice, and visual access.
Objective-wise advantage decoupling plus prefix-based marginal utility estimation improve multi-objective credit assignment.
evidence_signal: The paper reports evaluation on five multimodal agent-memory benchmarks, with preference sweeps producing broader performance-cost-latency frontiers than prior trade-off-aware baselines.
watch_item: The approach adds policy complexity and may be sensitive to reward design, model routing choices, and the compute overhead of multi-step runtime decisions.
paper_title: MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents
